title: The 3:00 AM Ferry to HarbourFront
subtitle: Reflections on the dark water between two countries, carrying a laptop and big ambitions.
quote: Crossing an international border by sea reminds you how arbitrary distances really are.
excerpt: Gliding across the dark Singapore Strait aboard a passenger ferry. Looking out the salt-streaked window at cargo ship beacons while clutching a backpack full of dreams and code.
body:
The twin diesel engines of the catamaran vibrated through the steel hull with a deep, hypnotic rhythm.

Outside the salt-filmed window, the water was inky black. We were slicing across the international shipping channel of the Singapore Strait—one of the busiest maritime arteries on the planet. Hundreds of colossal container ships and crude oil tankers were anchored across the water, their deck cranes and red navigational beacons glowing like floating cities.

Inside the cabin, the air conditioning was ice-cold. Most passengers were asleep, heads propped against vinyl headrests.

Between Two Worlds

I clutched my canvas backpack against my chest. Inside was my trusty laptop, a worn notebook, my passport, and a presentation deck for a software engineering conference in Singapore.

Growing up in the Riau Islands, you live in the constant shadow of a global metropolis. You can see the high-rises of the financial district on clear afternoons, yet between here and there lies a border, a passport stamp, and forty minutes of open sea.

"The ocean doesn't care about passports. It only asks whether your vessel is sturdy enough to handle the swells."

I opened my laptop lid and reviewed the architecture slide. The microservices were solid. The API contracts were cleanly decoupled. The test coverage was at 94%.

As the ferry rounded the southern tip of Sentosa, the glittering towers of HarbourFront and Marina Bay rose from the sea like a mountain of glass and light. I took a deep breath, zipped up my jacket, and smiled. The boat was docking. It was time to show the world what we could build.
